doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Woodstock, MCA and the Standards Trio
title: Inflation Blues, "Ebony" and the Bratislava jam
summary: The 1982 Special Edition record, a Compost-era piece reworked with ska horns, Ahmad Jamal covering "Ebony", and a 1983 festival jam.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’m going to return to your recordings and projects as a leader. Inflation Blues, Special Edition. This one has new personnel. Baikida Carroll on trumpet, Chico Freeman, John Purcell, so this is when you had again a three horn frontline and then again Rufus Reid on bass. The recording I know you mention that Howard Johnson had played tuba, so the band is in flux, but this recording. . . Inflation Blues recorded in New York, September, 1982 for ECM. “Starburst,” “Ebony,” “The Islands,” “Inflation Blues,” “Slowdown.” Anything about this one? Because after talking about this we’re going to go to the Standards because in the chronology that’s when the Standards project started up with Keith.
Right, then I think we come back to Special Edition later.
Oh sure! I’m following the chronology of the discography.
I’d originally written... “Inflation Blues” was recorded with Compost originally if you look on the titles.
Well, I can. Was it for Life Is Round, the second?
No, I think it was on Take Off Your Body, I think.

Was that all in one session, those two albums? The discography doesn’t give recording dates. It actually says “1971/1972.” They don’t even have any dates. I can’t even nail down the exact year, so I’m not sure.
We’ll check when we take a break.
But it’s something you had written during the Compost era? That would put it over ten years earlier.

I recorded it a couple of times, and I actually changed the name of it but we’ll get to that later. That comes up in the chronology. It’s a reggae kind of piece. I arranged the horns for it, like ska kind of arrangements.
Ska tempo?
But I had the horns doing [sings a ska horn line]. There’s something on there called “Ebony”, right?
Mm-hmm.

That one was a good piece, which I played piano (on), again this is where I overdubbed piano and then drums because I felt it would add something to the piece. This piece actually, “Ebony,” Ahmad recorded, piece of mine that he recorded on one of his records.
I hope you’re getting some royalties for that!
Yeah, but he really did a nice version of it.

Then if we could just wrap up with Special Edition, I’m showing the Bratislava Jazz Festival of 1983. This one had Marty Ehrlich, John Purcell, Howard Johnson, Rufus Reid and yourself and it’s just one cut. “Tenor Madness” recorded in Czechoslovakia October 1983.
Really?
[Laughs].
Now I remember when Marty Ehrlich was with me… “Tenor Madness”? Was Frank Foster on that? Because there was a jam session we played at a festival and I
think Frank Foster was playing too.
Well it’s entirely possible.
It’s just one tune?
That’s the only one that’s credited here. Like you said it was a jam session. Were you in the rhythm section for the entire jam session?
No, we just played a few numbers. But who knows?
So, we’re going to go ahead and take a break. HOUR 6
